title: The Unstable Patient: An ABCDE Bedside Approach
subject: Emergency Triage
preview: ABCDE stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability and Exposure; reassess after every intervention.
quickRevision: ABCDE stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability and Exposure; reassess after every intervention.
Disability includes conscious level, pupils and bedside glucose; exposure looks for bleeding, rash, trauma and temperature-related threats.
Use a team approach with closed-loop communication, early escalation and definitive help when instability persists.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: ABCDE stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability and Exposure; reassess after every intervention.
An obstructed airway, severe hypoxemia or massive bleeding threatens life before detailed diagnostic labeling.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Disability includes conscious level, pupils and bedside glucose; exposure looks for bleeding, rash, trauma and temperature-related threats.
Use a team approach with closed-loop communication, early escalation and definitive help when instability persists.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: ABCDE: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure — then reassess.
Prioritize life-threatening abnormalities while simultaneously calling for appropriate assistance.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Treat the life threat identified at each step rather than completing the alphabet before intervening.

quiz.question: What should be assessed first in an unstable patient using ABCDE?
quiz.explanation: Airway patency. ABCDE stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability and Exposure; reassess after every intervention.
